input.strategy_title: Graduate Llama Stack to General Availability
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Llama Stack shipped as Tech Preview and adoption is strong, but enterprise
customers will not build production GenAI applications on a TP component.
Graduating to GA requires API stability commitments, a production support
posture, and closing the quality gaps that TP status currently excuses. The
full inventory of those gaps is not yet known — TP feedback is scattered across
support tickets, and no systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), producing the definitive GA scope. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Published API surface carries a stability guarantee: versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases. |
| HLR-3 | P0 | Production support posture is in place: documented SLO targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix. |
| HLR-4 | P1 | Safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions. |
| HLR-5 | P1 | The Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate). |
| HLR-6 | P2 | Documentation is uplifted to GA standards, including migration notes from TP. |

## Affected Components

- Llama Stack
- TrustyAI
- Dashboard

## Out of Scope

- New Llama Stack feature development beyond GA-bar quality work
- Deprecating alternative GenAI serving paths

## Open Questions

1. The GA scope itself depends on HLR-1's assessment — until it lands, the
   size of the stability and hardening work is an estimate.

# Llama Stack GA-readiness assessment and definitive GA scope

## Description

This epic resolves the strategy's central unknown: the full inventory of gaps
between Llama Stack's current Tech Preview quality and the General
Availability bar. TP feedback is scattered across support tickets and no
systematic GA-readiness assessment has been done. This investigation
consolidates that feedback with a technical audit of the distribution and
produces the definitive GA scope that all stability, hardening, and support
posture work is planned against.

## Scope

- Collect and consolidate TP feedback from the support ticket corpus and other
  feedback channels (issues, escalations, field reports).
- Audit the current distribution against the four GA-bar inventory areas named
  by the strategy:
  - **API stability** — current API surface state, versioning posture, and
    stability risks on the OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and the
    LlamaStackDistribution CRD.
  - **Upgrade paths** — what upgrades between TP releases currently work,
    break, or are untested.
  - **Scale limits** — characterize current known limits (or explicitly mark
    them unknown) for the distribution at production-representative scale.
  - **Error handling** — audit error surfaces, failure modes, and observability
    of failures against the GA bar.
- Classify each identified gap as GA-blocking or non-blocking, with severity
  and owning area.
- Produce the **definitive GA scope document**: which gaps are in scope for
  GA, which are deferred with rationale, and the resulting size estimate for
  the stability and hardening work.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A gap inventory exists that covers all four inventory areas (API stability,
  upgrade paths, scale limits, error handling), with each gap classified
  (GA-blocking / non-blocking), severity-assigned, and traceable to evidence
  (ticket, test result, or code audit finding).
- The TP feedback corpus has been systematically reviewed, not sampled; the
  inventory states the corpus coverage.
- Scale limits are characterized with measured or evidence-backed values, or
  explicitly marked unknown with a characterization plan.
- A definitive GA scope document is published that states which gaps are in
  GA scope, which are deferred with rationale, and the resulting scope for
  the stability, hardening, and support-posture work.
- The GA scope document is delivered to the strategy stakeholders for
  acceptance.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)**: GA-readiness assessment inventories the gaps between
  current TP quality and GA bar (API stability, upgrade paths, scale limits,
  error handling), producing the definitive GA scope — this epic is the full
  delivery of HLR-1.

# Llama Stack API stability guarantee and GA hardening

## Description

This epic delivers the published API stability guarantee for Llama Stack's GA
surface and closes the quality gaps the GA-readiness assessment identifies.
It takes the distribution from "quality gaps excused by Tech Preview status"
to the GA bar on the same surface: versioned APIs, a deprecation policy, a
tested upgrade path from the last two TP releases, and remediation of the
GA-blocking gaps in error handling and other assessment-identified areas.

## Scope

- Version the published API surface (OpenAI-compatible REST APIs and the
  LlamaStackDistribution CRD) so GA consumers can pin against stable versions.
- Author and publish a deprecation policy covering the GA API surface.
- Build and test the upgrade path from the last two TP releases to the GA
  version, preserving distribution configuration and state across upgrades.
- Close GA-blocking quality gaps identified by the readiness assessment
  (error handling and the other inventory areas), or get them explicitly
  deferred with rationale in the GA scope.
- Fold the TP-feedback remediation items that the assessment places in GA
  scope into this hardening pass over the distribution.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The published GA API surface is versioned, and a deprecation policy document
  covering that surface is published.
- Upgrade from each of the last two TP releases to the GA version is tested,
  with test evidence that distribution configuration and state are preserved;
  failures are fixed or the incompatibility is documented in the migration
  notes with a workaround.
- Every GA-blocking gap in the assessment's inventory is closed or explicitly
  deferred with rationale recorded against the GA scope.
- Error handling on the distribution meets the GA bar as characterized by the
  readiness assessment.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P0)**: published API surface carries a stability guarantee —
  versioned APIs, deprecation policy, and a tested upgrade path from the last
  two TP releases — delivered by this epic.
- Assessed gap-closure scope from HLR-1's inventory is absorbed here as one
  hardening pass over the same distribution surface.

## Risks / Notes

- Scope is an estimate until the GA-readiness assessment lands; this epic is
  gated on that assessment and its scope is rewritten by its findings.
- Re-split trigger: if the assessment's gap inventory exceeds the
  stability-mechanics work in volume, split the remediation items into
  separate hardening epics by area.

# Llama Stack production support posture

## Description

This epic puts the production support posture in place for Llama Stack GA:
documented SLO targets, a backport policy, and a supported configuration
matrix. It converts the component from a Tech Preview support stance (best
effort, no commitments) to a GA support stance with defined targets and a
statement of which configurations Red Hat supports.

## Scope

- Define and document SLO targets for the GA distribution (the targets the
  support organization commits to and measures against).
- Define and document the backport policy: which releases receive fixes, for
  how long, and how fixes are selected.
- Define and publish the supported configuration matrix: the distributions,
  providers, dependency versions, and scale envelopes that are supported at
  GA, reflecting the scale limits characterized by the GA-readiness
  assessment.
- Align the posture documents with the platform's existing GA support
  standards so Llama Stack is supportable by the standard production support
  channels.

## Acceptance Criteria

- SLO targets for the GA distribution are documented and stated in measurable
  terms.
- The backport policy is documented, covering supported releases, fix
  selection criteria, and duration.
- The supported configuration matrix is published and reflects the scale
  limits and provider/configuration constraints validated in the
  GA-readiness assessment.
- The support posture documents are reviewed and accepted by the support
  organization and product stakeholders.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-3 (P0)**: production support posture in place — documented SLO
  targets, backport policy, and supported configuration matrix — delivered by
  this epic.

## Risks / Notes

- The supported configuration matrix portion of this epic is gated on the
  GA-readiness assessment (scale-limit characterization); SLO and backport
  policy work can proceed independently once the epic starts.

# TrustyAI guardrails as a supported Llama Stack distribution integration

## Description

This epic promotes the TrustyAI safety-guardrails integration for Llama Stack
distributions from an experimental flag to a supported, documented
integration. At GA, customers must be able to configure TrustyAI guardrails
on a Llama Stack distribution as a first-class supported path — part of the
GA distribution surface, covered by the stability guarantee and support
posture, not gated behind an experimental opt-in.

## Scope

- Promote the TrustyAI guardrails configuration path in Llama Stack
  distributions from experimental-flag status to a supported integration:
  the provider wiring, configuration surface, and default behavior expected
  of a GA-supported integration.
- Ensure the integration's configuration surface is versioned and covered by
  the distribution's deprecation policy.
- Exercise the integration functionally (guardrails applying to distribution
  traffic, expected failure behavior when TrustyAI is unavailable) so the
  promotion is evidence-backed, in coordination with the TrustyAI team's
  validation of the integration.

## Acceptance Criteria

- TrustyAI guardrails can be enabled on a GA Llama Stack distribution as a
  supported configuration path — no experimental flag or opt-in gate is
  required.
- The integration's configuration surface is versioned and covered by the
  distribution's deprecation policy.
- The promoted guardrails configuration surface — enablement steps, supported
  configuration options, and behavior when the guardrails service is
  unavailable — is handed to documentation as engineering input for the GA
  documentation uplift.
- Functional evidence exists that guardrails apply to distribution traffic in
  the supported configuration, and failure modes are handled per the
  distribution's error-handling bar.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration (not an experimental flag) for GA distributions — this epic
  delivers the distribution-side half: the promoted, supported integration
  and its versioned configuration surface. The documented-integration half
  is delivered by the GA documentation uplift, which authors the guardrails
  configuration topic from the configuration surface this epic hands over.

## Risks / Notes

- Cross-team coordination with the TrustyAI team is expected for validation
  and compatibility statements; the TrustyAI team's validation effort is
  tracked as its own work item.

# TrustyAI validation of the guardrails integration for GA distributions

## Description

This epic is the TrustyAI team's validation of the TrustyAI guardrails
integration with Llama Stack GA distributions. TrustyAI itself is already a
GA component and requires no code changes for this strategy; its role is to
validate and certify, from the TrustyAI side, that the guardrails integration
shipped in Llama Stack GA distributions is supported — functionally correct
against representative TrustyAI configurations, with documented compatibility
and support boundaries.

## Scope

- Define and run a validation suite exercising the guardrails integration
  across representative TrustyAI service configurations and Llama Stack
  distribution setups: functional behavior, configuration handling, and
  failure modes (guardrails service unavailable, misconfiguration).
- Document the TrustyAI-side compatibility and support statement for the
  integration: which TrustyAI versions/configurations are supported with GA
  distributions, and known limitations.
- File and escalate integration defects found during validation to the
  distribution owners, and re-validate fixes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A validation report exists covering the exercised configurations, with
  pass/fail results for functional behavior, configuration handling, and
  failure modes.
- All defects found during validation are filed against the owning teams, and
  blocking defects are resolved and re-validated.
- The TrustyAI-side compatibility and support statement for the integration
  is documented and published (supported versions/configurations, known
  limitations).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P1)**: safety guardrails via TrustyAI are a supported, documented
  integration for GA distributions — the TrustyAI-team validation and
  support-statement half of this requirement.

## Risks / Notes

- This work cannot start before the distribution-side integration promotion
  is available to validate.

# Dashboard Llama Stack management enabled by default for entitled clusters

## Description

This epic makes Llama Stack management available by default in the Dashboard
for entitled clusters, removing the Tech Preview opt-in gate. Today users must
opt in to see Llama Stack management surfaces; at GA, entitled clusters get
the management experience out of the box.

## Scope

- Change the Dashboard's Llama Stack management enablement from an explicit
  opt-in gate to default-on for entitled clusters, using the existing
  per-component feature-flag/default mechanism (OdhDashboardConfig).
- Ensure non-entitled clusters see no change: the management surfaces remain
  unavailable where there is no entitlement.
- Verify the Llama Stack management surfaces (navigation, resource views,
  status) work against the current LlamaStackDistribution CR surface.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On an entitled cluster, Llama Stack management is enabled in the Dashboard
  by default with no opt-in action required.
- On a non-entitled cluster, Llama Stack management surfaces are not shown,
  with no errors or broken navigation.
- The default-on behavior can be reverted to disabled via the existing
  feature-flag configuration (OdhDashboardConfig) without a code change.
- The management surfaces render correctly against the current
  LlamaStackDistribution CR surface (list, status, and detail views).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-5 (P1)**: the Dashboard enables Llama Stack management by default for
  entitled clusters (no TP opt-in gate) — delivered by this epic.

## Risks / Notes

- Because this change replaces the existing opt-in behavior, a rollback path
  is required and captured as an acceptance criterion above (feature-flag
  revert).

## Description

This epic uplifts the Llama Stack documentation to GA standards and authors
the migration notes that take customers from Tech Preview to GA: what changed,
how to upgrade, and what the new support posture and stability guarantees
mean for them. The documentation describes what was actually built, so it runs
last and is technically reviewed against the implementation.

    configuration path.

    clusters.

  behavior by engineering, with review evidence recorded.

  outline item 5), authored from the configuration surface handed over by
